notes: Star identifier HVS (also called the HVS candidate): it is the only supplied star explicitly assessed as completely unbound from the Milky Way (T:p6-b6, T:p7-b10, T:p9-b1), and the paper retains it as a hypervelocity-star candidate subject to future proper-motion checks. The supplied Table 1 excerpt (T:p7-b0) shows only six membership-"a" Sgr-stream rows and omits the membership-"d" HVS row, so no APOGEE/catalog identifier for this star is recoverable from the supplied material. The Sgr-stream, accreted-halo, bulge, and "others" stars are placed on bound calculated orbits and do not meet the Galactic-unbound criterion.

HVS: The target is the single hypervelocity star candidate among the Sgr chemical candidates (membership code d in Table 1). The paper gives no explicit parallax or distance value for it, only that its distance error is ~15%. Its v_gsr = -111 km/s is a Galactic-standard-of-rest velocity component and is not treated as a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity. The paper describes the star as completely unbound but reports no numerical bound/unbound probability.
